title: Slow and Full
about: Find what is slowing a device down, and free up space safely.

cards.prompt: Your laptop got slower all afternoon. Let's find out which part is struggling.

steps.text: What first? The [[task manager]] shows what each app is using.

choices.text: Open the task manager to see what's busy

choices.consequence: Booster apps rarely help, and some are junk or worse. Find the cause first.
That's a very expensive way to close 30 tabs. Find the cause first.

steps.text: [[RAM]] is **97% full**, with **30 [[browser]] tabs** open. What's the simplest fix?

choices.text: Close the tabs you don't need
choices.consequence: Each tab uses RAM. Fewer tabs, and the laptop speeds up!

choices.text: Delete some photos to make room
choices.consequence: Photos are in storage. The problem was RAM, so nothing changes.

cards.explanation: Look first, then fix. **Full RAM** meant closing tabs; deleting files only frees **storage**.
cards.hint: Find out what's busy first, then fix the part that's full.

cards.title: The fix-it loop
cards.body:
Good fixers use a loop:

1. **Describe** what's wrong: "slow with 30 [[tabs|browser-tab]] open" is a clue; "it's broken" isn't.
2. **Guess** the likely cause.
3. **Try** the simplest, safest fix.
4. **Check** it worked. If not, guess again.

cards.prompt: Your friend's laptop crawls with lots of tabs open. Put the fix-it loop in order.

items.label: Notice it's slow only with many tabs
Guess that the RAM is full
Close the tabs you don't need

cards.explanation: **Describe, guess, try, check.** The clue points to RAM, closing tabs is the fix, and checking shows if it worked.
cards.hint: You can't guess before describing, or check before trying.
cards.nudge: Start with what you notice; end with seeing if it worked.

cards.prompt: Laptops cool through **vents**. If the [[CPU]] gets too hot, it slows itself down (**throttling**).

steps.text: On your duvet, with two tabs open and lots of free storage, the fan roars and it all slows. Why?

choices.text: The duvet blocks the vents, so the CPU overheats
choices.consequence: Yes. The heat can't escape, so the CPU throttles.

choices.text: The two tabs have filled up all the RAM
choices.consequence: Two tabs use only a little RAM. What does a roaring fan tell you?

choices.text: The videos are filling up the storage
choices.consequence: There's plenty of free storage. What does a roaring fan tell you?

choices.text: Move it to a hard, flat table
choices.consequence: Air flows again, the CPU cools, and it speeds back up.
The screen isn't what's overheating: the duvet still blocks the vents.

choices.text: Close all your tabs to cool it down
choices.consequence: Only two tabs were open, so that barely helps. The duvet still blocks the vents.

cards.explanation: A roaring fan and a slowdown point to **heat**. Soft things block the vents; a hard, flat surface lets it breathe.
cards.hint: Clues: few tabs, lots of storage, a roaring fan. What does the fan cool?

cards.prompt: Free up **15 [[GB|gigabyte]]** or more. Keep your photos and essay.
cards.explanation: The game plus the old setup files (left over from installing apps) free 15 GB, and so do the backed-up videos alone. Photos and the essay stay.
cards.hint: Look for big things that are [[backed up|backup]] or never used.
cards.nudge: Keep photos and the essay; delete big unused or backed-up things until the meter hits 15.

cards.prompt: Delete what's backed up, **duplicated** or unused; keep **only copies**, things you need and **system files**.

items.label: Leftover installers for apps you have
Five blurry copies of the same photo
Your only copy of family photos

cards.explanation: Backed-up, duplicated or unused things can go (an app can be reinstalled). Keep **only copies**, things you need and **system files**, which the device needs to run.
cards.hint: Is it backed up, a duplicate or unused? Or an only copy, needed, or a system file?
cards.nudge: Only copies, things you still need and system files are risky to delete.

cards.prompt: Your laptop takes five minutes to start, then crawls for a while after.

steps.text: The [[task manager]]'s **Startup** list shows **15 apps** that open when it switches on. Likely cause?

choices.text: Too many apps starting at once
choices.consequence: Yes. They all fight for the [[CPU]] and [[RAM]] at once.

choices.text: The screen is set too bright
choices.consequence: Brightness affects the battery, not how fast the laptop starts.

choices.text: Stop the apps you don't need from starting
choices.consequence: They still work when you open them. They just don't all start at once.

choices.text: Stop the security app from starting up
choices.consequence: That's the one to keep. It protects you from the moment you log in.

choices.text: Delete the system files that load first
choices.consequence: Then the laptop might not start at all.

cards.explanation: Turning off **startup apps** you don't need speeds up starting. Keep the security app, and never delete system files.
cards.hint: What happens when lots of apps open at the same moment? And which one protects you?

cards.prompt: Free **12 GB** for an [[update]]. Keep your **only copies**.
cards.explanation: Music (in the cloud), backed-up videos and maps (re-downloadable) free enough. Your photos are the **only copy**, so they stay.
cards.hint: Read each label: no adding up needed, the free space meter does the maths.
cards.nudge: Keep the **only copy** files; look for ones in [[the cloud|cloud]], [[backed up|backup]] or re-downloadable.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Use the loop: **describe, guess, try, check**.
- **Slow?** Too many [[tabs|browser-tab]] fill [[RAM]]. Heat makes the CPU slow down.
- **Full?** Delete what's backed up or unused. Keep your only copies.
